limitations: Clock-only instrumentation adds overhead. Refresh-only runs deliberately abort at Chromium launch after completed refresh and generation validation; their failed sentinel reports are retained, not counted as acceptance.

Durations are nested wall spans and must not be summed. Native gzip duration includes native queue/wait. Bootstrap/restart pool health jobs are excluded. Legacy projection build was not instrumented, so no isolated parallelism benefit or penalty is quantified.
Linux four-CPU quota; no Chromium workload or PASS connection. Each server uses a private copy of the same completed 30k demo seed.

Controlled route A/B on the same runtime: before installs the exact three production route bodies from 8c575ecd parent at compilation through a diagnostic-only external preload. All dependencies, authority, pool warmup and observer are otherwise identical. Repository files are not modified.
Cold means first metadata request in a fresh process/file-cache generation; it is not cold OS disk cache. Subsequent MAG and Buyer Group first requests already share that index.
Both servers automatically warm the existing common pool at startup as production does; no extra artificial pool warmup is added.
Latency includes loopback HTTP, automatic gzip decoding and client JSON parsing. Requests are sequential with no retries; none send refresh. BL_STALL_PROFILE is unset in both arms.
